about: One sample per run-pipeline tool branch, each also carrying ride-along paths, so a few detonations exercise every tool. Branches are exclusive (chosen by the input's type), so the floor is one sample per branch. A sample is kept only if a real run passes every predicate in `expect` (report-shape.py). Build it out over time; see ADR-031.

samples.note: Native PE (no branch); runs encoded PowerShell. Report 21ab9faaeeaf. Covers path.powershell_from_behaviour: the script sample did not run PowerShell in the guest.

samples.select: A native (non-.NET) loader whose .NET payload CAPE actually extracts in THIS guest: check a candidate's past CAPE runs (CAPE/, procdump/, selfextracted/ holding a PE with a CLR header) before detonating. The payload path runs only for native inputs; its code is unit-tested with synthetic extractions (test_header_peeks_hostile, test_dotnet_carve_never_follows_links), so only a real sample is missing.

samples.note: VBA Word template. Ran on the office guest; macros extracted. Report 19de1dd78328 (stub profile, 2026-11-24).
JS loader. Took the script branch, but ran no PowerShell in the guest, so path.powershell_from_behaviour stays with native-powershell. Report c7f2cb9b3f49.
Python 3.13; extracted and decompiled. Report 41e6d8d91b15. The first pick (5702cb05..., Python 3.14) took the branch but pycdc rejected its bytecode (Bad MAGIC): a tool gap, not a sample problem.

samples.select: A .ps1 loader given as the input itself. Optional: the same tool already runs on PowerShell decoded from behaviour.
